description: The search snippet highlight() function lowercases both haystack and needle for case-insensitive matching, but builds parallel char-index tables (lower_chars, orig_chars) to map match positions in the lowercased string back to the original. A contributor might simplify to byte-offset arithmetic (abs_lower_idx used directly on the original). But Unicode lowercasing can change a character's byte length (some characters expand or change byte width), so a byte offset into lower_haystack is not a valid byte offset into the original haystack. The char-index table approach is the only correct general-purpose solution.
title: highlight() in MemoryBackend builds char-index tables to correctly map lowercased match positions back to original string
